offence_severity: Death caused by the accused, which is punishable under Section 302 IPC (life imprisonment)
physical_harm: The deceased sustained firearm injuries in the chest and died. The accused sustained minor injuries such as bruises and contusions.
number_of_offences: Multiple charges were filed, but the High Court upheld the conviction of the appellant under Section 302 IPC and acquitted others.
premeditation_planning: The court found that the accused acted aggressively and without premeditation, and their actions were not in good faith.
key_evidence_accepted: The evidence showed that the complainant party neither used fire arms nor any fire arm was found in their possession. The injuries on the person of the accused were not so serious. The complainant and his brothers were not carrying any arms or deadly weapons.
witness_credibility: PW1-Bharat Singh, PW5-Anil Kumar and PW6-Gajraj have clearly spoken about the occurrence, they were consistent in their version despite searching cross-examination and their evidence is trustworthy. Further, evidence of eye-witnesses is strengthened by the medical evidence.
trial_duration: The trial judgment was passed on 17.05.2008, the High Court decision was on 30.01.2013, and the Supreme Court decision was on 23 April 2015.
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Amit Anand Tiwari; Counsel for the State: S. Gurukrishna Kumar, B. K. Satija, AAG, Vivek Singh, A. Prasanna Venkta, Gagan Gupta, Kamal Mohan Gupta
investigation_status: FIR registered on 321/2004, charge sheet filed under Sections 323, 324, 302, 307 and 506 read with Section 341 IPC, trial completed

appeal_history.trial_court: Appellant-Raj Singh convicted under Section 304 Part-1 IPC, acquitted Rajpal and Rishi Pal
appeal_history.high_court: Dismissed the Criminal Appeal of the appellant-Raj Singh, allowed the Criminal Revision, converted conviction under Section 304 Part-1 IPC to Section 302 IPC, maintained life imprisonment sentence
appeal_history.supreme_court: Confirmed the conviction and sentence of Raj Singh under Section 302 IPC, dismissed appeals

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused, Raj Singh, fired shots at the deceased, Girdhari Lal, which resulted in his death, and that the complainant party were not armed with lethal weapons, thus the act of firing was not in self-defense. The prosecution also contended that the place of occurrence was the house of the accused, and that the complainant party were aggressors.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the accused, Raj Singh, acted in self-defense as the complainant party were aggressors who had entered his house and were armed with weapons, causing injuries to his brothers. The accused claimed that he had a reasonable apprehension of harm and thus fired the shots in self-defense.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the right of private defence does not extend to causing death unless the offender acts in good faith, without premeditation, and without any intention of doing more harm than is necessary for the purpose of such defence. The court also emphasized that the right of private defence is available only when there is a reasonable apprehension of danger.
precedent_relied_upon: Dharam And Ors. vs. State of Haryana, 2006(10)Suppl. SCR 391 : (2007) 15 SCC 241; Bhanwar Singh & Ors. vs. State of M.P. 2008 (9) SCR 1 : (2008) 16 sec 657; Biran Singh vs. State of Bihar AIR 1975 SC 87, Wassan Singh vs. State of Punjab 1995 (5) Suppl. SCR 703 : (1996) 1 SCC 458, Sekar alias Raja Sekharan vs. State represented by Inspector of Police, T.N., 2002 (3) D Suppl. SCR 113: (2002) 8 sec 354, Buta Singh VS. State of Punjab, AIR 1991 SC 1316 and James Martin vs. State of Kera/a 2003(6) Suppl. SCR 910: (2004) 2 sec 203
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence of life imprisonment was imposed because the court found that the accused, Raj Singh, was the aggressor and that his act of firing shots was not in self-defense. The court concluded that the accused had no right to claim the benefit of Exception 2 to Section 300 IPC and that his actions were not justified under the law.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The court weighed that the accused acted aggressively, fired shots recklessly from a close range, and that the act of firing was not to prevent any injury which could have been reasonably apprehended. The court also noted that the accused was armed with a pistol while the complainant party were not armed with lethal weapons.
